URL corrected this pass: the legacy www.indianbank.in domain 502s on every path (decommissioned); on indianbank.bank.in itself the old '/departments/deposit-rates/' path is now a dead end (302s to a path that then 502s) — the current canonical page is '/en/deposit-rates' (confirmed via a real browser session landing there with the matching title 'Deposit Rates - Maximize Your Savings - Indian Bank', and via an Internet Archive id_ snapshot of exactly that URL dated 2026-09-17). format is 'browser' because this exact page sits behind an F5 BIG-IP ('TSPD') bot-defense layer: plain HTTP from this sandbox (curl and this project's own fetchDoc, with or without a same-origin Referer header, and with a full realistic browser header set) always gets either a flat 502 or a small obfuscated-JS challenge page, never the real table markup, whereas a real browser session and the Internet Archive crawler both reached the genuine page — so a headless browser (Playwright, as GitHub Actions/VPS already run for other 'browser' sources) should render it. The fixture was captured live on 2026-09-27: its retail-table date (04.08.2026) and rates (e.g. 1 year = 6.10%, IND Supreme 2.0/300d = 6.20%) independently match the Internet Archive snapshot exactly. No RD source: the page's senior-citizen rule text says the same senior addition 'similarly' extends to Recurring Deposit accounts for a 6-120 month band, which is evidence RD has its own card, not evidence its base rate equals the FD card rate — no RD rate table or an explicit 'RD = FD' statement appears anywhere on the page, so RD rates are not published on the official site. Separately (not implemented this pass, flagged for follow-up): the page explicitly states "The rate of interest on domestic term deposit is also applicable to IB Tax Saver Scheme and Capital Gains Scheme Type B (Term Deposits) 1988 Scheme" — a genuine tax_saver-from-FD gap.

Caveat found while confirming: this project's own fetchDoc -- specifically its self-identifying User-Agent string (contains 'FixedReturnTracker/1.0 (+https://github.com/...)') -- reliably hangs to a DOMException timeout against this URL from this sandbox, while the identical request with an ordinary browser User-Agent (no other header changed) succeeds in under a second, repeatedly; this looks like a stealth anti-bot rule keyed on the UA string rather than a general site outage (the previous engineer's own notes already flagged this bank's PDFs as slow to download). Not yet known whether GitHub Actions' UA/IP is treated the same way -- worth reconfirming there rather than assuming it behaves identically to this sandbox.
